content: Tailwind CSS v4 uses CSS-first configuration via the @theme directive: theme variables like --color-* are defined in CSS and automatically generate matching utility classes (e.g., bg-primary-500). This is the recommended integration path for a Material 3 design system: map Material 3 tonal palette roles (primary, secondary, tertiary, surface, inverse-surface, error, etc.) to @theme variables, then use those utilities in components. The --*: initial syntax can disable the default Tailwind palette if a strict M3 palette is desired. Theme variables are also emitted as CSS custom properties, so dynamic theming (light/dark) is done by changing the values of those variables in CSS, not by runtime class manipulation.
